text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PROD inference-service - 5xx-rate-spike (P1)
incident-bot: Alert details: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345 — error rate > 5% sustained for 3m, auto-group: inference-5xx-eu
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: page sent to maria_oncall (ack pending)

maria_oncall: ack — I'm on it, picking up the page now.
maria_oncall: quick snapshot: K8s autoscaler hasn't flapped, but nginx upstream 502/503s spiking in eu-west-1.
chris_ops: seeing the same in Datadog — spike started ~14:01 UTC, correlated with a burst of long-running token-generation requests.

sam_t: any customer-impact reports? which tenants?
maria_oncall: two customer support tickets from enterprise-accounts in EU mentioning intermittent model timeouts; CS escalated at 14:04.

kevin_infra: re: paging storm — we've got 24 PD incidents auto-grouped under inference-5xx-eu. Looks like duplicate pages from two alert rules firing (http_5xx_ratio and proxy_timeout_rate). We should silence duplicates and adjust the incident-bot dedupe window.

maria_oncall: putting an emergency silence for 30m while we triage to stop noise. Command:```bash
# PagerDuty CLI
pdc incidents silence --service PROD-inference --duration 30m --reason "triage + stop storm"
```

pagerduty-bot: Silence created: PROD-inference (30 minutes) by maria_oncall

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/inference/runbooks/5xx-spike — recommended steps: (1) check model queue depth (2) verify cache/kvs hit rates (3) route to fallback-quantized model if latency > 3s

maria_oncall: following runbook — checking queues and KV cache.

maria_oncall: KV cache hit rate dropped from 94% -> 57% at spike. Prefix cache miss rate climbed. That explains backend load.

chris_ops: evidence in logs:```json
{"ts":"2026-07-05T14:02:17Z","level":"ERROR","msg":"model inference timeout","model":"gpt-j-6b","latency_ms":12034,"request_id":"req_9f3b"}
```

sam_t: can we route traffic to fallback model-variant: gpt-j-6b-quant? That one is cached more aggressively and tolerates load.

kevin_infra: I can flip routing for EU on the traffic-router for a soft-failover. Doing TTL=60s and canary 20%. Command:```bash
curl -X POST https://router.internal/route -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER" -d '{"service":"inference","region":"eu-west-1","target":"gpt-j-6b-quant","weight":20}'
```

kevin_infra: applied canary 20% to gpt-j-6b-quant at 14:12 UTC. Monitoring.

maria_oncall: metrics: 5xx rate dropped from 7.8% -> 3.1% after canary, KV hit rate recovering to 78%. Good sign.

chris_ops: continuing to see duplicate PD pages from the other rule even though we silenced service-level — looks like per-rule alerts still firing. Suggest updating incident-bot suppression to dedupe rules from same symptom for 5m.

maria_oncall: agreed. Kevin, can you update incident-bot autogroup/suppression? Current config: group_by: [service, region, alert_name]. Increase grouping window and add "suppress_if_group_exists: true".

kevin_infra: on it. Pushing a quick config change:```yaml
incident-bot:
  autogroup:
    window_seconds: 300
    suppress_if_group_exists: true
    min_unique_alerts: 1
```

kevin_infra: config pushed at 14:18 UTC. Watch for fewer duplicate pages.

pagerduty-bot: Alert dedupe applied; suppressed 16 duplicate pages.

maria_oncall: confirming: we've silenced noise, routed traffic to fallback, KV hit rate trending up. Any next escalation?

chris_ops: still seeing a few long tail timeouts, but customer impact contained to small percentage of requests. Recommend severity downgrade to P2 after 14:25 if error rate stays <2.5%.

maria_oncall: agreed — I'll keep monitoring. Scheduling handoff: I need to step out for stand at 14:30 UTC. Sam, can you take follow-up on-call if this stays noisy? ops-rota-bot, please note handoff.

ops-rota-bot: handoff noted. maria_oncall -> sam_t at 14:30 UTC.

sam_t: taking over at 14:30. I'll keep the silence and continue monitoring dashboards and PD.

kevin_infra: follow-up change: increased autogroup window and bumped the per-rule alert threshold from 3->6/min to avoid paging storms caused by short spikes. Pushed at 14:27.

maria_oncall: quick post-incident customer note draft: "We observed elevated 5xx rates in EU due to cache churn leading to backend timeouts. Traffic was temporarily routed to a fallback quantized model while caching recovered; the issue is mitigated. Our engineering team will update runbooks and adjust alert grouping to prevent repeat paging storms." Thoughts?

chris_ops: looks good, add note that impacted customers were routed automatically and SLA degradation was minimal.

sam_t: current status at 14:40 UTC: 5xx = 1.1%, KV hit = 92%, PD pages suppressed, canary scaled back to normal routing. I'll keep monitoring for 1h and then close the thread if stable.

maria_oncall: thanks team. Action items: [kevin_infra] update incident-bot config permanently and open a PR, [sre-runbook-bot] update runbook with new suppression guidance, [sam_t] watch metrics and file incident report.

kevin_infra: opening PR now: https://git.internal/infra/incident-bot/pulls/342 — includes autogroup window change + suppression flag.

sre-runbook-bot: Created runbook task: update runbook and add a note about silencing and grouping (task id RB-887).

sam_t: will submit incident report and recommend retro with CS to review customer communications.

maria_oncall: resolving my PD ack and removing emergency silence at 15:00 if stable. Final note: this was a good example of multi-alert duplication + cache churn; changing grouping rules should reduce cognitive load for on-call. :thumbsup:

ops-rota-bot: maria_oncall has cleared the emergency silence at 15:00 UTC (silence expired).

sam_t: closing monitoring window at 15:30 UTC, will link incident report once created.

maria_oncall: thanks everyone — great coordination.
